ac_suggestions: ac3 username clause is self-contradictory as written: it requires test_duplicate_username_raises_integrity_error to reject a DIFFERENT-CASE second username ('same' then 'SAME') while calling that 'proving case sensitivity'. Under SQLite BINARY collation a plain UNIQUE treats 'same' and 'SAME' as DISTINCT (probed on the worktree's locked SQLite: both inserts are accepted); rejecting different-case values would prove case-INsensitivity, contradicting REQ-DB-011 and the groom's own discriminator ('a wrongly-collated implementation fails'). The only DB mechanism that rejects 'same'/'SAME' is a lower()-based functional unique index, i.e. exactly the NOCASE-style behavior t6 lists as out of scope. Implemented reading (pinned node ID and pinned command unchanged, rc=0): the test asserts an exact-case duplicate username raises IntegrityError AND that a different-case username is accepted — which genuinely exercises BINARY collation and would fail a wrongly-collated implementation. Suggest Definer reword the clause at the next re-groom.
